signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + BoJ Hawkish Shift
signals.text: CAD/JPY trades under heavy pressure as JPY leads the G10 scorecard with a +1.674% weekly average, while CAD lags at -0.973%. The BoJ July meeting minutes reveal members are increasingly attentive to upside price risks and signal that inflation is set to rise significantly in the second half of the fiscal year. This hawkish shift coincides with JPY ESI at +22.9, confirming that realized economic data is consistently outperforming expectations. While CAD/JPY carry remains at +125bp, the institutional positioning in JPY is extremely short (LF net -124,575), creating a massive technical vacuum for a squeeze as the BoJ pivots. Options markets are aggressively pricing for further JPY strength, with EUR/JPY 25d RR at -2.71 showing an extreme downside skew. Risk: BoJ fails to follow through with a rate hike in September, allowing the carry trade to re-establish.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitics + Carry vs Options Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY at 157.66 is holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (162.09/161.28/157.97), signaling a technical breakdown despite the 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage. Iran's rejection of US claims regarding the Strait of Hormuz has introduced acute geopolitical tension, supporting JPY demand while the market digests hawkish Fed commentary from Schmid regarding tighter policy. A massive divergence has emerged between CFTC specs (LF net short -124,575) and the options market, where the 25d RR at -2.76 reflects the strongest downside hedging demand in the G10. This institutional skew suggests the 'carry first' regime is failing as VIX trades at 16.5 and risk-off headlines accumulate. Further downside targets the recent 155.20 base if geopolitical rhetoric escalates. Risk: US 10Y yields rebound sharply above 4.70%, re-asserting the USD carry dominance over safe-haven flows.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence + ESI Outperformance
signals.text: NZD/USD is trading at 0.5871, positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5803/0.5792/0.5827) in a clean bullish technical setup. A significant divergence is active: CFTC LF net positioning is extremely short at -30,606 (long% 9.7%), yet the RBNZ is actively in a HIKING cycle with a positive OIS bias for the September 2nd meeting. NZD ESI leads the complex at +33.4, showing the strongest data beat in the G10, which fundamentally contradicts the crowded speculative short. This setup creates an asymmetric risk profile where any further hawkish RBNZ signaling triggers a forced cover of the spec shorts, targeting a move toward 0.6000. Retail sentiment provides a contrarian tailwind as 75% of retail traders are short, chasing the move lower. Risk: RBNZ pivots to a hold stance on September 2nd, validating the speculative short thesis.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Volatility Premium + Positioning + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD is trading at 0.7046, testing resistance just above its SMA50 at 0.7009. The pair exhibits the highest Vol Risk Premium in the G10 majors at +6.7%, with IV at 12.8% significantly outpacing HV30 at 6.1%, indicating the options market is paying a heavy premium for protection. This high vol-cost environment is typical of late-cycle moves where participants are hedging against a trend reversal rather than chasing it. While the 70bp AONIA-SOFR carry favors AUD, the ESI at -13.9 suggests Australian data is beginning to miss expectations, creating a fundamental headwind. A notable multi-layer divergence exists where COT LF is net long +23,616 while retail sentiment is 74% short, signaling that retail is fading the institutional trend. Risk: AUD/USD closes below the SMA200 at 0.6915, invalidating the bullish structure.
evidence: AUD COT net: +23,616 vs Retail 74% short
